title: Glacier Idol — K-Pop Mini Album Booklet
description: A mini album booklet layout built around a bilingual Hangul-above/English-below name lockup, a 3–4 member concept-photo grid, an oversized centered sans-serif album title, and a tracked monospace tracklist — distilled directly from HYBE's NewJeans and Le Sserafim art direction.
philosophy: This template exists to translate the precise editorial grammar of K-pop physical releases into a slide format without diluting its identity. It refuses the horizontal Western title-bullet hierarchy, instead treating the bilingual name lockup and concept photography as co-equal structural pillars — not decoration, but the brand statement itself. Every typographic choice defers to the logic of the printed booklet: oversized title as emotional anchor, monospace tracklist as quiet counterweight. It is built for creative agencies, idol management teams, and music label directors who must present visual concepts with the same authority and finish as a pressed photobook.
goodFor: K-pop group concept or comeback reveal presentations
Music label artist pitch decks anchored by high-quality member headshots
Album pre-release or teaser slide packages for fan communities
Creative agency portfolios showcasing idol visual identity systems
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly financial reviews requiring dense data tables
Academic research summaries or paper presentations
Presentations with no professional concept photography assets
Corporate investor decks where bilingual typographic hierarchy reads as off-brand
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide reads as a pressed K-pop album cover: glacial, still, and quietly authoritative. Compositional weight is shared equally between the full-bleed idol photography and the centered typographic architecture — neither element is decoration for the other. The oversized title acts as an emotional anchor that grounds the coldness of the image, while the bilingual lockup above it signals brand precision and group identity. Avoid warmth, informality, or Western editorial looseness — the mood is considered restraint, like a photobook left open to its very first page.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed concept photo occupies the entire slide field as a base layer with zero outer margin on any edge. A 12-column grid sits atop it: the bilingual Hangul-above/English-below name lockup is centered across cols 4–9, anchored in the upper third with tight internal leading between the two language lines. The oversized album title runs horizontally across the visual center of the slide as the primary typographic mass, hierarchy achieved through scale contrast alone rather than weight or rule lines. A single tracked monospace release label sits flush to the bottom edge — no header band, no page number.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a spread torn from a pressed K-pop physical booklet — glacially cool, editorially precise, and quietly intimate. Compositional tension lives in the asymmetry between the dense, saturated photographic mosaic on the left and the spare, vertically breathing typographic column on the right; neither side dominates, they hold each other. The monospace tracklist functions as a counterweight — understated and structural, not decorative. Avoid any visual language that signals Western corporate slides: no bullet hierarchies, no banded headers, no generic layout symmetry.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with a 3–4 cell concept-photo mosaic occupying cols 1–7 in an asymmetric portrait/landscape split, bleeding flush to the left edge with no margin. Bilingual name lockup — Hangul line primary, fine hairline rule, English line secondary — anchors the upper portion of the right column (cols 8–12) against an 8% outer margin. Tracked monospace tracklist stacks beneath the lockup with generous leading, left-aligned to the column axis and running toward the bottom third of the slide. No decorative header band; folio number sits bottom-right outside the live area.
